//: Per-route MINIMUM Persian digit counts for lumo-gate's persian-digit-floor rule. Each floor is ~55% of the count measured on 10 Aug 2026, so a redesign can shrink a page without going red while a page that silently stops rendering its numbers — the defect the rule exists for — cannot pass. Routes chosen because numbers are their point: the landing's proof figures, the number-dense component pages, and the composed dashboard.
//dates: Calendar grids are the densest Persian-digit surface in the library — a month of day cells. Floored at ~55% of the 10 Aug measurement so a layout change can shrink the grid without going red, while a calendar that reverts to Latin day cells (the defect that started this library) cannot pass. The other date routes carry 10-18 digits of chrome rather than data and are deliberately unfloored: a floor on incidental digits breaks on the next copy edit and teaches people to weaken floors.
